focus: The CI workflow inventory: duplicate guards, report-only jobs, and scope mismatches
noveltyJustification: 5 of 6 findings are fully new and 1 is partially new, because the trigger-index overlap touches the settled efficiency packet.
keyQuestions: Which CI workflows duplicate a local git hook check or another workflow, and how many seconds per run would deleting or merging them save?
ruledOut: Re-arguing triggers, caching or consolidation (settled in 002-ci-workflow-efficiency)

graphEvents.label: Which workflows duplicate a hook or another workflow
Advisory checks are green by construction

label: Twenty-six of the 32 workflows trigger on both push and pull_request, so every duplicated guard pays its cost twice per change.
Five workflows re-run a check the local hooks already block: comment hygiene, agent mirror sync, prompt card sync, message contract and routing registry drift.
advisory-checks.yml runs four continue-on-error report-only steps, is green by construction, costs 87 s mean per run, and states in its own comment that its run status must not be read.
The doc-model validator removed from pre-commit for being advisory landed in that report-only job, so it now cannot block locally or in CI.
The trigger index has two owners: an advisory --check on every push and PR, and a 185 s rebuild workflow that repairs the same artifact after merge.
dispatch-enforcement-guard.yml carries a job named Every hook vitest suite passes that runs the whole .skilled/hooks vitest tree, so a workflow named for one guard can fail for unrelated reasons.

direction: Deleting the hook-backstop CI workflows outright
reason: Each covers the uninstalled-hook case that a fresh clone hits; the saving is in run frequency, not deletion.
